Laminated paper is not fire-safe; the film can melt or trap moisture [T02:Seed Backup Copies and Materials]. Don't count on the lamination to protect it — keep it away from heat and damp, and plan to re-secure the words on proper backup material before moving anything.

[T02:BIP-32 hierarchical deterministic wallets] Whoever holds it can watch your addresses and balances, but cannot spend.

**Does it matter which one you give your accountant?**
- For safety: no. Neither one is a spending secret.
- For correctness: yes. You will see these codes in wallet settings, export files and backup tools. If you keep written notes about your wallet, note the path as well. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase] If their software imports the key with the wrong path, it can show an empty balance, because the wallet is checking different addresses than the ones holding your bitcoin. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase] So give the export that matches your wallet's addresses — if your addresses start with bc1, the zpub is the right one.

These codes are hierarchical deterministic derivation paths — instructions that tell a wallet which addresses to generate from a seed. m/44, m/49 and m/84 correspond to different address formats: m/44'/0'/0' produces Legacy (addresses starting with 1), m/49'/0'/0' produces wrapped SegWit (addresses starting with 3), and m/84'/0'/0' produces native SegWit (bc1 addresses). [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]

The path is a tree with five levels, like folders inside folders; a spot in the tree is written m / 44' / 0' / 0' / 0 / 0, and the first address of the first Bitcoin account sits at path m/44'/0'/0'/0/0. [T02:BIP-44 multi-account hierarchy]

A seed phrase does not by itself fix the address type; the wallet must be told, or must scan, which path to derive, which is why backups should record the path used at creation. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]

Restoring a seed with the wrong path can show an empty balance, because the wallet is checking different addresses than the ones holding your bitcoin. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]

For native SegWit (m/84) accounts specifically, the scheme is not backwards compatible by design: an incompatible wallet will not discover these accounts at all. [T02:BIP-84 bech32 addresses]

## Your situation

- Your hardware wallet showing m/84'/0'/0' is that device's own setting — the path that produces native SegWit (bc1) addresses. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]
- Your father's note of m/44' suggests his wallet used the Legacy format (addresses starting with 1). [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]
- These are different address formats. When restoring his wallet, his noted path is the one that matters. If a restore ever shows an empty balance, the wallet may be checking different addresses than the ones holding the bitcoin — in other words, the wrong path. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]

## DO

- Write down the derivation path (for example m/84) in your offline notes so a future restore derives the same addresses. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]
- Keep his original notes with your written wallet records. You will see these codes in wallet settings, export files and backup tools; if you keep written notes about your wallet, note the path as well. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]
- Keep all of this on paper, offline.

## DO NOT

- Do not assume the seed words alone are enough — a seed phrase does not by itself fix the address type. [T02:Derivation paths and why you must not photograph your seed phrase]
- Do not photograph the seed phrase or store recovery details in cloud-connected apps: modern mobile systems commonly enable full-library cloud backup by default, and a photographed seed phrase should be treated as exposed the moment the shutter fires.
